pages.title: Operating your cold room
pages.panel: Almost every cold room fault we are called to attend comes from one of three things: a door left open, air blocked at the evaporator, or hot product loaded straight in. All three are avoidable at no cost.
body: KEEP THE DOOR CLOSED. Every time the door opens, warm humid air enters and turns into ice on the evaporator and frost on the floor. Open it, go in, close it. Do not prop it open while loading — stage the goods outside and move them in one trip. Where a strip curtain is fitted, keep it complete and hanging straight; a missing strip is a permanently open door.

LEAVE AIR SPACE. Cold air has to circulate. Do not stack goods against the evaporator, under its discharge, or tight to the walls and ceiling. Leave a clear gap all round and keep the fan discharge unobstructed. A blocked evaporator raises the room temperature even though the unit is running normally.

DO NOT LOAD HOT PRODUCT. Let cooked or freshly delivered warm product cool before it goes into the room. Hot product raises the room temperature, puts the compressor under sustained load, and adds moisture that becomes ice.

DO NOT CHANGE THE SETTING. The thermostat has been set for the product this room is intended to hold. If your storage requirement changes, call us and we will reset it — do not adjust the controller on site.

LEAVE THE UNIT RUNNING. Do not switch the room off overnight or at weekends to save electricity. The product warms, moisture condenses, and the compressor is stressed by repeated cold starts. After any power failure, allow a few minutes before restarting so pressures can equalise.

CLEAN CAREFULLY. Use a mild detergent and a damp cloth on panels and floor. Never pressure-wash the panels, the evaporator, the control panel or any electrical enclosure. Keep the floor clear of standing water and ice — it is a slip hazard and usually a sign of a door or drain problem.

DO NOT MODIFY THE STRUCTURE. Do not drill, screw into, or hang shelving or loads from the insulated panels. Do not run cables or pipework through them. Any penetration breaks the vapour seal and causes condensation inside the panel that cannot be seen until the insulation has failed.

REPORT EARLY. Unusual noise, ice building up, water on the floor, or a temperature drifting away from its normal reading are all early signs. Called in early they are a service visit; left alone they become a breakdown and a load of spoiled product.

pages.title: Routine checks for your team
pages.intro: These take a few minutes and are the difference between a small correction and a breakdown. Assign them to a named person and keep a simple temperature record.

rows: Room temperature against its normal reading
The earliest warning of any developing fault
Door closes fully and the gasket seals all round
The single largest cause of ice and lost temperature
Floor clear of water and ice
Slip hazard, and a sign of a door or drain problem
Strip curtain complete and hanging straight
A missing strip is a permanently open door
Ice restricts airflow and raises room temperature
Nothing stacked against the evaporator or blocking airflow
Blocked air circulation warms the room while the unit runs
Condenser coil clear of dust, boxes and obstruction
A blocked condenser trips the unit on high pressure
Door gasket, hinges and closer condition
Drain line clear and draining freely
A blocked drain puts water on the floor and ice in the room
Temperature records reviewed for any drift
A slow trend is visible in the record long before it is visible in the room

pages.note: Keep the temperature record. If a fault is ever disputed, the record is what shows how the room was operated.

pages.title: 12 month warranty — what is covered
pages.intro: TNDK warrants the equipment and materials supplied and installed under LPO PO-2026-0000248, and the workmanship of that installation, for 12 months from the date of handover — 11 August 2026 to 11 August 2027. Two items are excluded and are shown in red below.

rows: Insulated wall, ceiling and floor panels

Control panel, thermostat and electrical wiring

pages.note: Door handles and lights are not covered under the warranty. They remain available from TNDK as chargeable replacement items — call the service number and we will supply and fit them.

pages.title: If there is a problem
pages.intro: Check the obvious first — it resolves a good proportion of call-outs in minutes. If it is not one of these, call us rather than waiting to see whether it settles.

rows: Door closed and sealing · nothing blocking the evaporator · condenser clear
Call TNDK. Move product if the rise continues
Ice on the evaporator or ceiling
Call TNDK. Do not chip or hammer ice off — the coil damages easily
Drain not blocked · door gasket sealing
Reset the breaker once. If it trips again, call TNDK and leave it off
Switch off and call TNDK immediately. Running a failing compressor destroys it
Frost on the outside of panels
Call TNDK — this indicates a vapour seal issue and should be seen quickly
